## Diagnosis

`set_key` (main.py:184-185) writes single-quoted values escaping only `'` → `\'`, but never escapes backslashes. The parser (parser.py:25, 32, 132) decodes `\\` and `\'` inside single-quoted values via `decode_escapes`. So a literal `\` written raw is misread: `\n` becomes newline, `\\` collapses to `\`, and a trailing `\` before the closing quote breaks parsing. Consecutive backslashes and apostrophes therefore fail to round-trip.

## Change Plan

In `set_key`, when quoting, escape backslashes first, then apostrophes: `value_to_set.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("'", "\\'")`. This matches the parser's single-quote escape set (`\\`, `\'`), so `dotenv_values(interpolate=False)` reproduces the exact value. `quote_mode` selection and `export` handling stay unchanged. No parser edits needed. Verify with tests covering single/consecutive backslashes, apostrophes, and mixed cases for both `always` and `auto`.
